newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain unveils proposed treaty change.
newsitem.headline: Britain unveils proposed treaty change.

text.p: Britain formally proposed on Tuesday that it be exempted from the European Union law on working hours by having the law made part of London's opt-out from EU employment policy.

In a formal text presented to inter-governmental conference (IGC) negotiators in Brussels, Britain said it wanted a protocol, or side agreement, added to the EU treaty saying that the law had been adopted under the so-called Social Chapter.
Britain can opt out of such laws following an agreement during the Maastricht Treaty negotiations.

The European Court of Justice on Tuesday rejected Britain's challenge to the law. Britain had argued that it should have been able to veto it, but the court ruled that the law was properly agreed under majority voting.
Britain also proposed various amendments to the treaty to ensure that what it sees as employment legislation cannot be agreed under more general treaty articles.
The working hours directive was approved as worker health and safety legislation, requiring a majority vote.

The proposal will join a growing number of others presented to the IGC by the EU's 15 member states. They will form part of the ongoing negotiations, which are due to end with a new treaty in June next year.
